source.title: Learning with AMIGo: Adversarially Motivated Intrinsic Goals

confidence_rationale: Directly on-point: a self-generated goal frontier solves hard procedurally-generated MiniGrid sparse tasks where count-based/RND-style bonuses stay at floor -- the unsupervised analogue of what BC achieved for REE. Moderate build (goal-proposer + goal-conditioned policy). Needs a parameterizable goal space.
failure_signatures: AMIGo/goal-generation assume a parameterizable goal space (e.g. (x,y) target cells); if the useful competence is not expressible as a reachable goal-state the curriculum cannot target it.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A goal-generating teacher network proposes target cells to a goal-conditioned student, rewarded (adversarially) for goals the student reaches in more than t* steps but not never -- keeping goals at the moving frontier of competence; this solves KeyCorridor/ObstructedMaze where IMPALA and count-based/RND intrinsic bonuses fail.
mapping.ree_translation: AMIGo is the unsupervised analogue of REE's competence-clearing BC arm: it manufactures a dense, self-paced achievable teaching signal WITHOUT an expert -- the 'unsupervised route to what BC (32.72) achieved' the floor->competent gap needs.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Wins are on navigation/reach tasks with (x,y)-parameterized goals; the REE forage competence must be reducible to a nameable reachable goal for the guarantee to transfer, and the teacher is a learned net (more than a one-line reward change).
mapping.source_context: Deep RL on procedurally-generated MiniGrid (KeyCorridor, ObstructedMaze), goal-conditioned IMPALA student.

confidence_components.notes: Cleanest discrete-gridworld precedent for an unsupervised competence-manufacturing signal; the goal-space precondition is the main transfer risk.
